subject: Numeracy
title: More and fewer
objectives: Children will say which of two groups has more or fewer.
Children will match objects one to one to check.
content: Which group has more, which has fewer, and matching one to one to check.
teachingActivities: Compare groups by matching objects one to one in two rows before counting; use the words more, fewer and the same; use real objects children care about such as sweets pictures, toy cars and fruit; avoid judging by how spread out a group looks.
learnerActivities: Say which of two groups has more or fewer and match objects one to one to check.
assessment: Observe whether each child says which group has more or fewer and checks by matching.
expectedOutcomes: Matches groups one to one to check.

lessons.title: Which has more?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say which of two groups has more.
successCriteria: Says more for the larger group
Points to the group with more
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have counted to 10, named numerals 1 to 10, sorted, compared size and length, and named three shapes.
resources: Two plates with different numbers of counters
Pictures of two groups of fruit
lessons.starter: Show two plates of counters and say "Which plate has more? Let us find out."
teacherActivities: Show two groups of counters with a big difference and ask which has more.
Show pairs of groups and ask each child to choose.
learnerActivities: Children point to the plate with more.
Child points to the group with more.
Child says it has more or looks bigger.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two groups of counters with a big difference and ask which has more. Children: Children point to the plate with more.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "This plate has more counters." Children: Children repeat more.
Step 3. Teacher: Show pairs of groups and ask each child to choose. Children: Child points to the group with more.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How do you know?" Children: Child says it has more or looks bigger.

practical.title: More or fewer plates
steps: Point to the one with more.
practical.safety: Use counters too large to swallow and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Compare groups with a very clear difference.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a group with more than the teacher’s group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the plates away and say more.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two groups of fruit and say which has more.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say which of two groups has more" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Which has fewer?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say which of two groups has fewer.
successCriteria: Says fewer for the smaller group
Points to the group with fewer
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have counted to 10, named numerals 1 to 10, sorted, compared size and length, and named three shapes.
resources: Two plates with different numbers of counters
lessons.starter: Show two groups of toy cars and say "One group has fewer cars. Which one?"
teacherActivities: Show two groups and ask which has fewer.
Compare more and fewer for different pairs.
Ask "Which has fewer, the red or the blue?"
learnerActivities: Children point to the smaller group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two groups and ask which has fewer. Children: Children point to the smaller group.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "This group has fewer." Children: Children repeat fewer.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare more and fewer for different pairs. Children: Child says more or fewer.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which has fewer, the red or the blue?" Children: Child points and says fewer.

practical.title: More or fewer cars
steps: Look at two groups of cars.
practical.safety: Use large toy cars and supervise closely so cars are not thrown. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Compare groups with a very clear difference and use the words together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a group with fewer than five.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cars away and say fewer.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two sets of toys and say which has fewer.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say which of two groups has fewer" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Matching to check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will match objects one to one to find which group has more.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have counted to 10, named numerals 1 to 10, sorted, compared size and length, and named three shapes.
lessons.starter: Put a car in each garage and say "Does every car have a garage? Let us match."
teacherActivities: Put red counters in a row and place blue counters below each.
Let children match cars and garages.
learnerActivities: Children point to the extra counters.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put red counters in a row and place blue counters below each. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "The red row has extra." Children: Children point to the extra counters.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children match cars and garages. Children: Child matches one to one.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Are there enough garages?" Children: Child says yes or no.

practical.title: Match and check
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep rows tidy on the mat.

differentiation.support: Match five counters with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to match ten counters and say how many extra.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say match.
lessons.homeConnection: Match cups to plates at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match objects one to one to find which group has more" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The same number
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find groups that have the same number.
successCriteria: Makes a group the same as another
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have counted to 10, named numerals 1 to 10, sorted, compared size and length, and named three shapes.
lessons.starter: Show two plates with five counters each and say "These plates have the same number."
teacherActivities: Show two equal groups and say same.
Give a group and ask children to make the same.
Check by matching one to one.
Play the same or different game.
learnerActivities: Child makes a group the same.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two equal groups and say same. Children: Children say same.
Step 2. Teacher: Give a group and ask children to make the same. Children: Child makes a group the same.
Step 3. Teacher: Check by matching one to one. Children: Child matches to check.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the same or different game. Children: Child says same or different.

practical.title: Make it the same
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Make groups of three or four with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make two groups with the same number and a third with one more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes a group the same as another
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say same.
lessons.homeConnection: Find two groups of objects that are the same.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find groups that have the same number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 more and fewer check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child compares groups.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have counted to 10, named numerals 1 to 10, sorted, compared size and length, and named three shapes.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: more, fewer and matching.
At each station ask "Which has more?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: more, fewer and matching. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which has more?" and watch. Children: Child answers and matches.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Compare stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use clear differences.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to make a group with two more.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says more; says fewer; matches one to one; makes a group the same.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child compares groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
